prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: a training gym with a heavy bag, ring ropes, a fencing strip and racks of weights
Outfit: a work shirt with rolled sleeves and jeans — in a soft pastel palette such as powder pink, baby blue, mint or lavender; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: walking.
COMPOSITION: a three-quarter shot from her head to just above the knees; body turned three-quarters away from the camera; head turned back over her own left shoulder — the shoulder on the image's left side; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP — on the image's right side, since her back is to the camera.
LEFT HAND: her own left arm hangs relaxed at her side — on the image's left side, since her back is to the camera.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a small banded violet-and-green fluorite crystal glowing faintly in her palm at chest height; it is all she holds.
LEGS: paused mid-walk, weight on the front foot.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: level lowered brow, steady unblinking eyes, mouth closed in a straight line, jaw set.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — fluorine: the most electronegative element of all, a pale yellow gas that tears electrons from almost anything it touches — glass, metal, water, even the aloof noble gas xenon; hydrofluoric acid that eats and frosts glass; banded violet-and-green fluorite crystals, named from 'fluere', to flow, for their use as a smelting flux, which in turn gave 'fluorescence' its name; first isolated by Henri Moissan in 1886 after it had injured the chemists who tried before him; yet the carbon–fluorine bond it forms is so tight that nothing sticks to Teflon; greedy, swift, ferocious — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
